input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 satisfies the preferred position on its material terms and comfortably clears the fallback. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual ("The cap is mutual"), set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000; "Fees" (1.5) means recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees payable under an Order Form, so the basis is meaningful rather than illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually ("neither Party is liable"), and helpfully confirms restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages. Section 21.3 places outside the cap each Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP — covering every carve-out we require. Two points are noted rather than redlined: the payment carve-out is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all Customer amounts due (taxes, expenses and interest are outside the "Fees" definition), and 21.2's exclusion is qualified "to the extent those damages are legally excludable"; neither is material given 21.4 (savings language, independent caps surviving failure of an exclusive remedy) and 18.2 (insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). No hidden or one-sided cap appears in the warranty (19.4) or indemnity (Section 20) provisions.
